name: Emparan-Horowitz-Myers Black Holes on a Brane
description: Exact black holes on a wall with two dimensions of space in anti-de Sitter space of four dimensions, found by Roberto Emparan, Gary T. Horowitz, and Robert C. Myers in 1999 by cutting the C-metric of anti-de Sitter space along a surface of constant extrinsic curvature and gluing it to a copy of itself. Far from the hole the wall approaches a cone, as gravity in three dimensions requires, and the mass of the cone equals the thermodynamic mass of the hole in four dimensions.
convention: Every coordinate is a pure number, with the lengths in the factor that multiplies the line element, and the Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\alpha\beta} = R^\gamma{}_{\alpha\gamma\beta}$.
history: One dimension down from the wall of Lisa Randall and Raman Sundrum, Roberto Emparan, Gary T. Horowitz, and Robert C. Myers solved Einstein's equations exactly [emparan2000branes, randall1999b]. Their wall has two dimensions of space and sits in anti-de Sitter space of four dimensions [emparan2000branes]. Randall and Sundrum's linear perturbations are singular on the horizon of anti-de Sitter space, and Emparan, Horowitz, and Myers asked whether that horizon stays regular with a mass on the wall [emparan2000branes]. Gravity in three dimensions with no cosmological constant has no black holes, and a point mass leaves the space around it flat, a cone with a deficit angle set by the mass [emparan2000branes]. Their solution is a black hole on the wall, with a horizon that reaches only a little way off it [emparan2000branes]. They posted it on 6 November 1999, and it was printed in January 2000 [emparan2000branes].¶They started from the C-metric of anti-de Sitter space, an accelerating black hole in the family Jerzy Plebański and Marek Demiański found in 1976 [emparan2000branes, plebanski1976]. A cosmic string along half of its axis pulls the hole, and they cut the spacetime along the surface $x = 0$, whose extrinsic curvature is its induced metric over the anti-de Sitter radius $\ell$ [emparan2000branes]. They kept the side with no string and glued it to a copy of itself, so that the surface became a wall of constant tension $1/(2\pi G_4\ell)$, with $G_4$ Newton's constant in four dimensions [emparan2000branes]. In a time $\hat t$ and a radius $r$ along the wall its metric is $-(1 - 2\mu\ell/r)d\hat t^2 + (1 - 2\mu\ell/r)^{-1}dr^2 + r^2d\varphi^2$, with $\mu$ the mass parameter of the C-metric, and its part in $\hat t$ and $r$ is Schwarzschild's [emparan2000branes]. Far from the hole the wall approaches a cone, as gravity in three dimensions requires, and the curvature singularity lies on the wall alone, at $r = 0$ [emparan2000branes]. Off the wall the field of the hole falls off as $1/z$ in the Poincaré coordinate $z$, and it vanishes on the horizon of anti-de Sitter space [emparan2000branes].¶Newton's constant on the wall is $G_3 = G_4/(2\ell)$ [emparan2000branes]. They read a mass $M_3$ off the deficit angle and a mass $M_4$ off the first law of thermodynamics in four dimensions, and found $M_3 = M_4$ for every $\mu$ [emparan2000branes]. The deficit angle cannot exceed $2\pi$, so $M_3$ stays below $1/(4G_3)$, and as $\mu$ grows the area of the horizon grows without bound: "arbitrarily large black holes can be produced from finite mass!" [emparan2000branes]. A large hole reaches a proper distance of about $\ell\log(2\mu)$ off the wall and a radius $2\mu\ell$ along it [emparan2000branes]. On a wall with three dimensions of space they expected corrections of order $\ell G_4M/r^2$ to Newton's potential $G_4M/r$, larger than the $\ell^2G_4M/r^3$ of Randall and Sundrum's linear analysis [emparan2000branes]. An exact hole there would need a C-metric of five dimensions, and "such a metric is not yet known", they wrote [emparan2000branes].¶Emparan, Horowitz, and Myers then gave the wall a negative cosmological constant, in a sequel of 15 December 1999, so that gravity on it has the black holes of Máximo Bañados, Claudio Teitelboim, and Jorge Zanelli [emparan2000branes2, banados1992]. A single wall curved like anti-de Sitter space leaves beside it a second asymptotic region, where the graviton bound to the wall cannot be normalised, so they cut the C-metric along $y = 0$ as well, and both walls have positive tension [emparan2000branes2]. At large masses the hole is a black string stretched between the two walls [emparan2000branes2]. On a weakly curved wall the string has the larger entropy down to $M_3 \approx 1/(32G_3)$, where its narrowest circumference is of order the anti-de Sitter radius [emparan2000branes2]. Andrew Chamblin, Stephen W. Hawking, and Harvey S. Reall had expected the instability of Ruth Gregory and Raymond Laflamme to break such a string at that size, and below that mass the hole on the wall has more entropy [chamblin2000, emparan2000branes2]. Set spinning on a flat wall, the hole induces there the equatorial geometry of Kerr's black hole, and for a small hole the angular momentum measured on the wall equals the one in four dimensions [emparan2000branes2].¶On a wall with three dimensions of space, Naresh Dadhich, Roy Maartens, Philippos Papadopoulos, and Vahid Rezania solved in March 2000 the equations induced on the wall alone [dadhich2000]. For a static metric those equations form "a closed system of equations on the brane" [dadhich2000]. The bulk enters them through the projection of its Weyl tensor onto the wall, and they found Reissner and Nordström's metric with no electric charge and a tidal charge from the fifth dimension in its place [dadhich2000]. With a negative tidal charge, "which is impossible in general relativity", the metric has one horizon, outside Schwarzschild's [dadhich2000]. They showed that a warped bulk $f(z)\left(dz^2 + ds^2\right)$ with that metric for $ds^2$ "cannot satisfy the bulk field equations for any" choice of $f$ when the tidal charge is not zero [dadhich2000]. Roberto Casadio, Alessandro Fabbri, and Lorenzo Mazzacurati found two more families in 2002, set by the mass and the post-Newtonian parameter $\beta$, with black holes regular everywhere for one sign of $\beta - 1$ [casadio2002].¶Emparan, Ruth Gregory, and Caroline Santos repeated the construction with no cosmological constant in 2001, where the wall is a sphere with a black hole at two opposite points, and smoothed it into a thick domain wall of scalar field [emparan2001thick]. On a wall with three dimensions of space, Hideaki Kudoh, Takahiro Tanaka, and Takashi Nakamura found small holes numerically in 2003 that flatten as they grow, and could not reach horizons as large as the anti-de Sitter radius [kudoh2003]. Mohamed Anber and Lorenzo Sorbo dropped in 2008 the tuning of the wall's tension to the acceleration of the hole, and found every way a wall of constant tension can sit in the C-metric of anti-de Sitter space [anber2008]. One class of their solutions is a lump of dark radiation that changes with time, and the other a pair of black holes held apart by a strut, "the first exact solution on the brane describing two objects in interaction" [anber2008]. Emparan and Giuseppe Milanesi kept in 2009 the other side of the surface $x = 0$ and found a black hole resting near the wall, whose dual under holography is a disk of plasma at finite temperature surrounded by vacuum [emparan2009plasma]. Robie A. Hennigar, Ayan K. Patra, and Simon F. Ross put a wall at $y = 0$ alone in 2026, and the geometry on it has no horizon and closes at a smooth origin [hennigar2026solitons].

related.text: The metric induced on the wall at $x = 0$ when the wall has a negative cosmological constant, with a term in $1/r$ from the fourth dimension [emparan2000branes2].

The accelerating black hole with no cosmological constant. With one, Emparan, Horowitz, and Myers cut its anti-de Sitter version along $x = 0$, and a wall takes the place of its cosmic string [emparan2000branes].

The same wall one dimension up, with three dimensions of space in anti-de Sitter space of five. There Emparan, Horowitz, and Myers expected corrections in $1/r^2$ to Newton's potential [emparan2000branes].

The black hole of three dimensions with a negative cosmological constant. A large hole on a wall curved like anti-de Sitter space induces it there exactly, as a black string stretched between two walls [emparan2000branes2].

A black hole stretched along an extra dimension. Between two walls in anti-de Sitter space of four dimensions such strings have the larger entropy at large masses, and holes localized on one wall have it below about $M_3 = 1/(32G_3)$ [emparan2000branes2].
At $\mu = 0$ each side of the wall is a piece of anti-de Sitter space of four dimensions, in Poincaré coordinates [emparan2000branes].
A point mass in three dimensions with no cosmological constant is a cone, and far from the hole the wall approaches one [emparan2000branes].
With $k = -1$ the metric induced on the wall at $x = 0$ is a slice through the equator of this black hole, and the mass on the wall is negative [emparan2000branes2].
Set spinning on a flat wall, the hole induces there the equatorial geometry of Kerr's black hole, and a small one has the same angular momentum on the wall as in four dimensions [emparan2000branes2].
With a tidal charge from a fifth dimension in place of the electric charge, Reissner and Nordström's metric solves the equations induced on a wall with three dimensions of space [dadhich2000].

coordinates.name: Flat Wall
domains: x = 0 \;\text{(the wall, where this side meets its mirror image)}
y = -1/(2\mu) \;\text{(the horizon of the black hole)}
y = 0 \;\text{(the horizon of anti-de Sitter space)}

parameters.description: Radius of anti-de Sitter space, a length, with $R_{\alpha\beta} = -(3/\ell^2)g_{\alpha\beta}$ on each side of the wall
Mass parameter, a positive pure number; the horizon $y = -1/(2\mu)$ meets the wall at the radius $r = 2\mu\ell$

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates $(t, y, x, \varphi)$ of Roberto Emparan, Gary T. Horowitz, and Robert C. Myers on one side of the wall, with $x_2$ the positive root of $1 - x^2 - 2\mu x^3$ and $\Delta\varphi = 2\pi/(x_2(1 + 3\mu x_2))$. On the wall the time $\hat t = \ell t$ and the radius $r = -\ell/y$ are lengths. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = \dfrac{\ell^2}{\left(x - y\right)^2}\left(-\left(y^2 + 2\mu y^3\right)dt^2 + \dfrac{dy^2}{y^2 + 2\mu y^3} + \dfrac{dx^2}{1 - x^2 - 2\mu x^3} + \left(1 - x^2 - 2\mu x^3\right)d\varphi^2\right)
geodesics: \ddot{y} + \dfrac{y^3\left(x + 3\mu\,y\,x - \mu\,y^2\right)\left(1 + 2\mu y\right)}{x - y}\dot{t}^2 + \dfrac{5\mu\,y^2 - 3\mu\,y\,x + 2y - x}{y\left(x - y\right)\left(1 + 2\mu y\right)}\dot{y}^2 - \dfrac{2}{x - y}\dot{y}\dot{x} - \dfrac{y^2\left(1 + 2\mu y\right)}{\left(x - y\right)\left(1 - x^2 - 2\mu x^3\right)}\dot{x}^2 - \dfrac{y^2\left(1 - x^2 - 2\mu x^3\right)\left(1 + 2\mu y\right)}{x - y}\dot{\varphi}^2 = 0

\ddot{x} - \dfrac{y^2\left(1 - x^2 - 2\mu x^3\right)\left(1 + 2\mu y\right)}{x - y}\dot{t}^2 + \dfrac{1 - x^2 - 2\mu x^3}{y^2\left(x - y\right)\left(1 + 2\mu y\right)}\dot{y}^2 + \dfrac{2}{x - y}\dot{y}\dot{x} - \dfrac{3\mu\,y\,x^2 - 5\mu\,x^3 + y\,x - 2x^2 + 1}{\left(x - y\right)\left(1 - x^2 - 2\mu x^3\right)}\dot{x}^2 + \dfrac{\left(1 - y\,x + \mu\,x^3 - 3\mu\,y\,x^2\right)\left(1 - x^2 - 2\mu x^3\right)}{x - y}\dot{\varphi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Two Walls
domains: x = 0 \;\text{(the wall that holds the black hole)}
y = y_0 \;\text{(the horizon of the black hole)}

parameters.description: Acceleration, an inverse length; the radius of anti-de Sitter space is $\ell_4 = 1/(A\sqrt{\lambda + 1})$, with $R_{\alpha\beta} = -(3/\ell_4^2)g_{\alpha\beta}$ between the walls
Mass parameter, a length, not negative; at $m = 0$ the space between the walls is a piece of anti-de Sitter space
A positive pure number; the wall $x = 0$ is curved like anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions of radius $\ell_3 = 1/(A\sqrt{\lambda})$

The sign $+1$, $0$ or $-1$; at $m = 0$ the wall $x = 0$ is anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions in global coordinates for $k = -1$, and the black hole of Bañados, Teitelboim, and Zanelli of zero mass for $k = 0$ and of positive mass for $k = +1$

coordinates.convention: We use Emparan, Horowitz, and Myers's coordinates $(t, y, x, \varphi)$ between the walls $x = 0$ and $y = 0$, with $x_2$ the positive root of $1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3$, $y_0$ the least root of $-\lambda + ky^2 - 2mAy^3$, and $\Delta\varphi = 2\pi/(x_2(3mAx_2 - k))$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = \dfrac{1}{A^2\left(x - y\right)^2}\left(\left(-\lambda + ky^2 - 2mAy^3\right)dt^2 - \dfrac{dy^2}{-\lambda + ky^2 - 2mAy^3} + \dfrac{dx^2}{1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3} + \left(1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3\right)d\varphi^2\right)
geodesics: \ddot{y} - \dfrac{\left(m\,A\,y^3 - 3m\,A\,y^2\,x - \lambda + k\,y\,x\right)\left(\lambda - ky^2 + 2mAy^3\right)}{x - y}\dot{t}^2 + \dfrac{5m\,A\,y^3 - 3m\,A\,y^2\,x + \lambda - 2k\,y^2 + k\,y\,x}{\left(x - y\right)\left(\lambda - ky^2 + 2mAy^3\right)}\dot{y}^2 - \dfrac{2}{x - y}\dot{y}\dot{x} - \dfrac{\lambda - ky^2 + 2mAy^3}{\left(x - y\right)\left(1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3\right)}\dot{x}^2 - \dfrac{\left(1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3\right)\left(\lambda - ky^2 + 2mAy^3\right)}{x - y}\dot{\varphi}^2 = 0

\ddot{x} - \dfrac{\left(1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3\right)\left(\lambda - ky^2 + 2mAy^3\right)}{x - y}\dot{t}^2 + \dfrac{1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3}{\left(x - y\right)\left(\lambda - ky^2 + 2mAy^3\right)}\dot{y}^2 + \dfrac{2}{x - y}\dot{y}\dot{x} - \dfrac{3m\,A\,y\,x^2 - 5m\,A\,x^3 - k\,y\,x + 2k\,x^2 + 1}{\left(x - y\right)\left(1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3\right)}\dot{x}^2 + \dfrac{\left(1 + k\,y\,x + m\,A\,x^3 - 3m\,A\,y\,x^2\right)\left(1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3\right)}{x - y}\dot{\varphi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Rotating
domains: x = 0 \;\text{(the wall that holds the black hole)}

parameters.description: Acceleration, an inverse length; the radius of anti-de Sitter space is $\ell_4 = 1/(A\sqrt{\lambda + 1})$, with $R_{\alpha\beta} = -(3/\ell_4^2)g_{\alpha\beta}$ off the walls
Mass parameter, a length, not negative; at $m = 0$ the spacetime off the walls is a piece of anti-de Sitter space
A pure number, not negative; at $\lambda = 0$ the wall $x = 0$ is flat far from the hole, and for $\lambda > 0$ it is curved like anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions
The sign $+1$, $0$ or $-1$; a flat wall has $k = -1$
Rotation, a pure number; at $\lambda = 0$ and $k = -1$ the wall $x = 0$ has the equatorial geometry of Kerr's black hole of mass $m$ and rotation parameter $a/A$

coordinates.convention: We use Emparan, Horowitz, and Myers's coordinates $(t, y, x, \varphi)$ of the rotating metric, with $x_2$ the least positive root of $1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3 + a^2\lambda x^4$. Points are identified along $\varphi \to \varphi + \Delta\varphi$ at fixed $t + ax_2^2\varphi$, with $\Delta\varphi = 2\pi/(x_2(3mAx_2 - k - 2a^2\lambda x_2^2))$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = \dfrac{1}{A^2\left(x - y\right)^2}\left(\dfrac{-\lambda + ky^2 - 2mAy^3 - a^2y^4}{1 + a^2x^2y^2}\left(dt + ax^2d\varphi\right)^2 - \dfrac{1 + a^2x^2y^2}{-\lambda + ky^2 - 2mAy^3 - a^2y^4}dy^2 + \dfrac{1 + a^2x^2y^2}{1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3 + a^2\lambda x^4}dx^2 + \dfrac{1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3 + a^2\lambda x^4}{1 + a^2x^2y^2}\left(d\varphi - ay^2dt\right)^2\right)

\dfrac{a\left(x^2\left(-\lambda + ky^2 - 2mAy^3 - a^2y^4\right) - y^2\left(1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3 + a^2\lambda x^4\right)\right)}{A^2\left(x - y\right)^2\left(1 + a^2x^2y^2\right)}
\dfrac{a\left(x^2\left(-\lambda + ky^2 - 2mAy^3 - a^2y^4\right) - y^2\left(1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3 + a^2\lambda x^4\right)\right)}{A^2\left(x - y\right)^2\left(1 + a^2x^2y^2\right)}
\dfrac{a^2x^4\left(-\lambda + ky^2 - 2mAy^3 - a^2y^4\right) + \left(1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3 + a^2\lambda x^4\right)}{A^2\left(x - y\right)^2\left(1 + a^2x^2y^2\right)}

-\dfrac{A^2\,a\left(2m\,A\,y^3\,x^2 - 2m\,A\,y^2\,x^3 + \lambda\,a^2\,y^2\,x^4 + \lambda\,x^2 + a^2\,y^4\,x^2 + y^2\right)\left(x - y\right)^2}{\left(1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3 + a^2\lambda x^4\right)\left(\lambda - ky^2 + 2mAy^3 + a^2y^4\right)\left(1 + a^2x^2y^2\right)}

-\dfrac{A^2\,a\left(2m\,A\,y^3\,x^2 - 2m\,A\,y^2\,x^3 + \lambda\,a^2\,y^2\,x^4 + \lambda\,x^2 + a^2\,y^4\,x^2 + y^2\right)\left(x - y\right)^2}{\left(1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3 + a^2\lambda x^4\right)\left(\lambda - ky^2 + 2mAy^3 + a^2y^4\right)\left(1 + a^2x^2y^2\right)}

\dfrac{A^2\left(2m\,A\,a^2\,y^4\,x^3 + 2m\,A\,y^3 - \lambda\,a^4\,y^4\,x^4 + \lambda - k\,a^2\,y^4\,x^2 - k\,y^2\right)\left(x - y\right)^2}{\left(1 + kx^2 - 2mAx^3 + a^2\lambda x^4\right)\left(\lambda - ky^2 + 2mAy^3 + a^2y^4\right)\left(1 + a^2x^2y^2\right)}
